title: Integration of Forms and the General Stokes Theorem

items.title: Compact support of a differential form
items.statement: For a smooth k-form omega, supp omega is the closure in M of its nonzero locus; Omega_c^k(M) consists of forms with compact support, also when M has boundary.
items.proof_plan: Intrinsic zero section and topological closure; do not identify support with the unclosed nonzero locus.

items.title: Local finiteness near compact support
items.statement: A locally finite family of closed supports meets a compact set K in only finitely many members, and all other members miss a neighborhood of K. Thus only finitely many rho_i omega are nonzero for compactly supported omega.
items.proof_plan: Cover K by finitely many neighborhoods witnessing local finiteness; take their union. This licenses all later sums and differentiation.

items.title: Riemann-integrable half-space extensions of chart coefficients
items.statement: For n>=1, a smooth coefficient compactly supported in a relatively open chart domain in H^n={x_n>=0} has a bounded compactly supported Euclidean zero extension, smooth off the genuine face and Riemann integrable. Its integral is independent of bounding rectangle and auxiliary smooth extensions. Interior charts give smooth zero extensions everywhere.
items.proof_plan: Finite Euclidean localization glues smooth extensions near the compact coordinate support; cutoff across artificial edges only. In a bounding cube of radius R, cover the face by O((R/delta+1)^(n-1)) cubes of side 2delta, total volume tending to zero. Apply the published null criterion. Two extensions agree on H^n.

items.title: Chart integral with its orientation sign
items.statement: For a compactly supported top form omega in a connected chart, write (phi^-1)^*omega=f dx^1 wedge ... wedge dx^n. Set its integral to sigma_phi times the Riemann integral of the zero-extended coefficient, where sigma_phi is the coordinate-frame orientation sign. For n=0 the chart is a point and the value is epsilon(p)omega(p).
items.proof_plan: The positive-chart case is the design formula. Negative charts are necessary at right interval endpoints; Lee p.405 explicitly explains this. Apply extension lemma before definition.

items.title: Local side-preserving extensions of half-space transitions
items.statement: A smooth diffeomorphism between relatively open half-space sets extends near any face point to a Euclidean local diffeomorphism that maps each side of the face to the corresponding side.
items.proof_plan: Inverse chain rule makes the derivative invertible. Tangential derivatives of the last component vanish on the face; the inward one-sided derivative is positive. Write the extended last component as t a(x,t) by the one-variable FTC, with a>0 after shrinking. Euclidean inverse theorem then supplies the extension and side equality. Needed before boundary change of variables.

items.title: Coordinate independence of chart integrals
items.statement: Assume AC_omega. The signed chart integral of a compactly supported top form is the same in any two charts containing its support, in all dimensions.
items.proof_plan: The determinant in the pulled-back top coefficient and sigma factors cancel the absolute Jacobian. At the boundary localize finitely into the Euclidean extensions in the preceding lemma and use Riemann change of variables on the zero-extended integrands; no contribution from the null face. For n=0 compare determinant-line signs.

items.title: Integral of a compactly supported top form
items.statement: Assume AC_omega. For n>=1, choose a subordinate smooth partition of unity in signed connected boundary/interior charts and sum the chart integrals of rho_i omega. For n=0 define sum_p epsilon(p)omega(p), where epsilon(p) records which of 1 or -1 is positive in the oriented determinant line; the sum is finite by compactness of a subset of a discrete manifold.
items.proof_plan: Partition existence assumes AC_omega; each actual sum is finite. Zero dimensions use no positive-dimensional integral.

items.title: Independence of atlas, partition and refinement
items.statement: Assume AC_omega. The integral defined above is independent of the cover, coordinate maps, partition and refinement; for support in an open subset it equals the integral computed there.
items.proof_plan: Refine rho_i and sigma_j by products. The finite double sum consists of chart-supported integrands; coordinate independence identifies every term. Same proof proves locality.

items.title: Linearity and additivity of the form integral
items.statement: Integration is linear; the integral is the sum over disjoint oriented connected components, only finitely many meeting the compact support.
items.proof_plan: Use one common partition. Components are open because manifolds are locally path connected, so compactness reduces their open cover to finitely many; treat zero-manifold by finite sums.

items.title: Orientation reversal changes the integral sign
items.statement: Replacing the orientation on every component by its opposite negates the integral, including determinant-line signs in dimension zero.
items.proof_plan: Every chart sign changes, as does every zero-dimensional point sign.

items.title: Positivity of the oriented integral
items.statement: A compactly supported smooth top form nonnegative on positive determinants has nonnegative integral, strictly positive if it is nonzero.
items.proof_plan: A nonzero nonnegative coefficient is bounded below by a positive constant on a small rectangle or half-rectangle; chart sign converts to the positive coefficient. For n=0 use signed coefficients on positive rays.

items.title: Change of variables on oriented manifolds
items.statement: For a globally orientation-preserving diffeomorphism F:M->N and omega in Omega_c^n(N), integral_M F*omega=integral_N omega; global reversal inserts minus. For varying signs across components apply the formula componentwise.
items.proof_plan: Pull back a subordinate partition and its charts. F^-1 maps compact sets to compact sets. Zero-dimensional case is a signed bijection of finite supports.

items.title: Integration on an oriented embedded submanifold
items.statement: For an oriented embedded k-submanifold j:S->M and a smooth k-form omega such that j*omega is compactly supported on S, define integral_S omega intrinsically as integral_S j*omega. It is unchanged by orientation-preserving reparametrization.
items.proof_plan: Compact support must be checked on S, not inferred for a nonproper inclusion. Pullback functoriality and change of variables give invariance.

items.title: Computing form integrals by finite parametrizations
items.statement: Let omega be a compactly supported smooth top form on an oriented n-manifold, n>=1. Suppose finitely many bounded open Jordan domains D_i have continuous maps F_i from their closures to M that are smooth up to the boundary in target coordinates (the coordinate representatives extend smoothly to Euclidean neighborhoods), restricting to orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms onto pairwise disjoint open W_i, and supp omega lies in the union of closures W_i. Then integral_M omega=sum_i integral_D_i F_i*omega.
items.proof_plan: Localize by finitely many small charts extending across genuine faces. Boundary images have chartwise content zero by the published C1 null-image lemma; apply finite almost-partition additivity and Jordan change of variables. This legitimizes circle cuts and fundamental polygons without invoking a manifold-with-corners theorem. Extension is of coordinate representatives, not an M-valued extension across a genuine boundary. This distinction includes the identity parametrization of a closed disk.

items.title: A signed one-density on a real vector space
items.statement: A real-valued function delta on ordered bases of an n-dimensional real vector space is a one-density if delta(v A)=abs(det A)delta(v); extend by zero to dependent n-tuples for n>=1. For n=0 it is a scalar on the empty basis. Real coefficients may be negative.
items.proof_plan: Separate the one-dimensional real density space from its nonnegative cone. No orientation is required.

items.title: The density line and its positive cone
items.statement: Densities form a one-dimensional real vector space, determined by their value on any basis; the nonzero nonnegative densities form one canonical positive ray.
items.proof_plan: Compare every basis to a fixed basis by a unique invertible matrix. This supplies the fiber for density-bundle gluing.

items.title: Density bundle and smooth density fields
items.statement: The density bundle has fiber D(T_pM), with local frame |dx^1...dx^n| and absolute-Jacobian transition law; a smooth density is a section with smooth local real coefficients. In dimension zero the bundle is canonically M times R.
items.proof_plan: Apply vector-bundle gluing to the positive nonzero absolute Jacobian cocycle. The proof that this gives a smooth line bundle is carried inline in the definition as its well-definedness explanation. Use a countable coordinate atlas and the published smooth cocycle construction; its chart gluing proof works unchanged for half-space charts.

items.title: Absolute value of a top form as a density
items.statement: Pointwise |omega| is a nonnegative continuous density, with |omega|=|-omega|. It is smooth wherever omega is nonvanishing; it need not be smooth at zeros (omega=x dx).
items.proof_plan: Use the determinant law and absolute value; |x| at zero is the regularity counterexample. This is not the linear signed correspondence below.

items.title: Existence of positive smooth densities
items.statement: Every smooth manifold with or without boundary has a smooth positive density, regardless of orientability.
items.proof_plan: Sum partition-weighted coordinate-frame densities. At least one weight is positive at every point and all coordinate densities are positive.

items.title: Pullback of densities by local diffeomorphisms
items.statement: For a local diffeomorphism F of equal-dimensional manifolds, F*(f|dy|)=(f o F)|det DF||dx| is smooth for smooth f, commutes with composition, and respects scalar multiplication.
items.proof_plan: The determinant is nonzero, so its absolute value is smooth locally. Do not assert smoothness for arbitrary maps: F(x)=x^2 pulls |dy| back to 2|x||dx|.

items.title: Integral of a compactly supported smooth density
items.statement: Integrate chart coefficients of compactly supported smooth densities by Riemann integration and sum a partition, with no chart-orientation sign. In dimension zero sum scalar coefficients over finite support.
items.proof_plan: Use true-face Riemann extensions as for forms, and global partitions as before; independence is proved in the next theorem.

items.title: Orientation-free density integration and its properties
items.statement: Density integration is independent of charts and partition, linear, local, positive on nonzero nonnegative smooth compactly supported densities, and invariant under all diffeomorphisms. The finite-parametrization formula holds with absolute Jacobians.
items.proof_plan: Repeat the product-partition proof with absolute determinants; positivity follows on a small coordinate rectangle. For parametrizations repeat the null-boundary additivity proof, without choosing orientations.

items.title: Orientation identifies top forms with signed densities
items.statement: A chosen orientation gives a linear smooth line-bundle isomorphism omega=f dx -> sigma_phi f |dx|, independent of chart and preserving compact support. Assuming AC_omega, it preserves the compact-support integral. At an oriented point send f to epsilon f. Reversing orientation negates this map.
items.proof_plan: Positive determinant comparisons give gluing; signed charts cover n=1 endpoints. This map keeps the sign of coefficients and is not omega->|omega|.

items.title: The separate measurable extension of density integration
items.statement: This page constructs only compactly supported smooth density integrals. Measurable nonnegative and L1 density integration, and associated Radon measures, belong to the Lebesgue/change-of-variables and regular-measure development.

items.title: Form calculus extends locally across a manifold boundary
items.statement: For smooth manifolds M,N with boundary, every smooth map F:N to M, every smooth vector field X on M, and every smooth form alpha on M, the coordinate exterior derivative, pullback naturality, support containment and Cartan identity hold. The graded Leibniz rule holds for homogeneous alpha of degree p and beta of degree q on M. Lie derivatives are defined by local Euclidean extensions at boundary points.
items.proof_plan: Use extensions and equality of all derivatives on the half-space. The usual local identities hold on extensions and restrict independently of choices; no two-sided boundary flow is required.

items.statement: For n>=1 and eta in Omega_c^(n-1)(R^n), integral_Rn d eta=0.

items.title: Localization of Stokes by a partition of unity
items.statement: For compactly supported eta, eta=sum_i rho_i eta and d eta=sum_i d(rho_i eta), with finite relevant sums; the d rho_i wedge eta terms cancel. Boundary restrictions form the corresponding finite localization.

items.title: The general Stokes theorem
items.statement: For an oriented smooth n-manifold with boundary, n>=1, and eta in Omega_c^(n-1)(M), integral_M d eta=integral_boundaryM j*eta with outward-normal-first boundary orientation. Empty boundary contributes zero.
items.proof_plan: Apply local Euclidean or half-space formula to each partition summand. Signed charts and their induced boundary signs match on both sides. Compact boundary restriction and finite localization discharge convergence.

items.title: Stokes agrees with the fundamental theorem of calculus
items.statement: Assume AC_omega. For [a,b] with increasing orientation and smooth f, the two signed boundary points give integral_[a,b] df=f(b)-f(a), agreeing with the published Riemann FTC.
items.proof_plan: The determinant-line boundary signs are -1 and +1; coordinate df is f prime dx. This is an agreement result, not a replacement for the FTC dependency in the local proof.

items.title: General Stokes agrees with both planar Green formulas
items.statement: Assume AC_omega. On the common smooth compact planar-region scope, d(P dx+Q dy)=(Q_x-P_y)dx wedge dy and d(P dy-Q dx)=(P_x+Q_y)dx wedge dy identify Stokes with published circulation and outward-flux Green formulas, using counterclockwise outer boundary and clockwise holes.
items.proof_plan: Compute d and match outward-normal-first with positive tangent; tangent (dx,dy) gives outward flux P dy-Q dx. Cite classical statements on their published elementary scope; no assertion that corners are already smooth manifolds.

items.title: Agreement of general and classical surface Stokes
items.statement: Assume AC_omega. For a smooth oriented compact surface with boundary in R^3, alpha=F_1 dx+F_2 dy+F_3 dz has d alpha=i_(curl F)(dx wedge dy wedge dz). Its pullback gives the classical normal curl flux and boundary circulation. On the common smooth patch scope this equals the published classical Stokes theorem.
items.proof_plan: Expand both expressions and evaluate on oriented tangent vectors to get (curl F) dot (r_u cross r_v); pull alpha to boundary curves for F dot r prime. Euclidean inner product identification is explicit.

items.title: Positive volume form on an oriented manifold
items.statement: A volume form is a nowhere-vanishing smooth top form positive on the chosen determinant ray. On an oriented zero-manifold this means epsilon(p)mu(p)>0.
items.proof_plan: No Riemannian metric is chosen; positive global top forms exist by the published orientation criterion, with local signs reconciled to the specified orientation.

items.title: Divergence relative to a volume form
items.statement: For a smooth vector field X and a positive volume form mu, div_mu X is the unique smooth function with L_X mu=(div_mu X)mu. At a boundary use the local-extension Lie derivative.
items.proof_plan: Top exterior power is one-dimensional and mu never vanishes, giving uniqueness; next result proves coordinate formula and smooth gluing.

items.title: Coordinate formula and well-definedness of divergence
items.statement: If mu=rho dx^1 wedge ... wedge dx^n with rho nowhere zero, then div_mu X=rho^-1 sum_i partial_i(rho X^i). This is a smooth globally defined function, including at the boundary. For n=0 X=0 and divergence is zero.
items.proof_plan: Cartan identity and degree n+1 vanishing reduce to differentiating i_X mu. Uniqueness of the scalar quotient makes the formula coordinate independent. No normal-flow assumption.

items.title: Product rule for volume-form divergence
items.statement: For smooth f and X, div_mu(fX)=df(X)+f div_mu X.
items.proof_plan: Expand partial_i(rho f X^i), divide by rho, and identify sum X^i partial_i f=df(X).

items.title: Divergence theorem for a volume form
items.statement: If M is oriented with boundary, dim M>=1, mu is a positive volume form and X is compactly supported, then integral_M (div_mu X)mu=integral_boundaryM i_X mu. If M is compact no support qualification on X is needed.
items.proof_plan: Contraction has support contained in supp X; apply general Stokes. Normal-flux formula for a general Riemannian metric is reserved for DG-18.

items.title: Agreement with classical Gauss flux in Euclidean space
items.statement: For a smooth field F on an open O in R^3, the Euclidean volume-form divergence and surface pullback have the usual scalar-divergence and cross-product formulas. Assuming AC_omega, on a compact smooth region E contained in O with standard orientation and supplied elementary-solid data, the two divergence theorems have identical volume integrals and boundary fluxes.
items.proof_plan: Compute contraction and pullback. Use identity parametrizations of the finitely many component interiors to identify the volume integrals, then apply both already-proved divergence theorems to identify the boundary values. Do not apply smooth finite-parametrization integration to merely C^1 classical boundary patches.

items.title: False: densities and top forms coincide on nonorientable manifolds
items.statement: False assertion: the canonical identification between top forms and densities exists without orientability.
items.proof_plan: The density bundle has a positive smooth section on every manifold; a nowhere-zero top form would orient it. For the Mobius band the transition determinant changes sign while its absolute value does not. In the explicit strip model, a putative nonzero top coefficient satisfies a(s+1,0)=-a(s,0), contradicting continuity and the intermediate value theorem on the central segment. Supply the two seam charts inline.

items.title: Partition weights in two overlapping charts
items.statement: For f in C_c^infinity((-1,1)), use charts x and y=2x on overlapping domains containing its support, and weights rho,1-rho. The two coordinate integrals sum to integral f dx independently of rho.
items.proof_plan: The second coefficient is (1-rho(y/2))f(y/2)/2. Substitute and add; choose a smooth partition on a neighborhood of the support and extend by unused charts outside.

items.title: A density integral on the Mobius band
items.statement: On the compact Mobius band (R times [-1,1])/((s,t)~(s+1,-t)), |ds dt| descends to a positive smooth density and its integral is 2.
items.proof_plan: Give quotient charts directly; seam transition has absolute Jacobian 1. Apply density parametrization formula to (0,1) times (-1,1); seam and boundary images are null. Reprove sign transition inline; no B-page dependency. Prove the quotient is Hausdorff using translations in the s-coordinate to separate inequivalent points, use a countable family of small rectangles for second countability, and show compactness as the image of [0,1] times [-1,1].

items.title: The angular period and the obstruction to bounding
items.statement: The angular form (-y dx+x dy)/(x^2+y^2) has oriented integral 2pi on the unit circle. Consequently that circle cannot bound a compact oriented smooth surface inside the punctured plane.
items.proof_plan: Compute d omega=0 inline, pull back to theta on a cut circle, apply finite parametrization. Previously published no-potential proof is acknowledged, not re-minted; the new conclusion is the bounding obstruction and intrinsic integral.

items.title: An exact top form with nonzero integral on a disk
items.statement: Assume AC_omega. On the standard-oriented unit disk, dx wedge dy=d(x dy) has integral pi, equal to the integral of its primitive x dy on the counterclockwise circle. The primitive is not an exact one-form.
items.proof_plan: Compute both integrals. Distinguish exact top form from its primitive: an exact (n-1)-form cannot have a nonzero integral on a compact boundary. This repairs the design's ambiguous exact-form-with-nonzero-boundary-integral example.
